criteria.description: Defines the decision criteria up front — minimum quality bar, latency budget, cost ceiling, and any hard constraints — before comparing models.
Recommends judging candidate models on the team's own task/eval set rather than relying solely on public benchmarks or general reputation.
Treats cost and latency quantitatively (e.g. $/request and p50/p95) at the stated volume, not as vague adjectives.
Applies the principle of choosing the cheapest/fastest model that clears the quality bar, rather than defaulting to the most capable model.
Compares candidates across tiers (e.g. frontier vs mid vs small, or considers a cascade/routing approach) rather than evaluating one option.
Includes a sensitivity analysis or re-evaluation trigger — what would change the recommendation (volume, price, quality bar).
Considers lock-in / portability or the need to re-decide as models change.
